title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第49部分：系统设计（二）：案例研究

chapters.Job: 12. 每天100万本书的那项任务
chapters.Frontier: 13. 前沿：设计如何失败，哪些仍属未知
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

41e37e015d4a.en: This part designs eight systems that almost everyone uses. <bookmark mark='a'/> A URL shortener, a news feed, a chat service and a web crawler. <bookmark mark='b'/> A ride-hailing dispatcher, a video platform, a payment ledger and a collaborative editor. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each one turns on a single hard idea, and every one of those ideas is something this series has already built: the birthday bound, fan-out, logical clocks, Bloom filters, the assignment problem, control loops, idempotency and CRDTs. Each design starts on a napkin and ends in a simulation.
41e37e015d4a.zh: 这一部分设计8个几乎人人都在用的系统。<bookmark mark='a'/>短网址服务、信息流、聊天服务和网络爬虫。<bookmark mark='b'/>网约车派单系统、视频平台、支付账本和协同编辑器。<bookmark mark='c'/>每一个都取决于一个困难的思想，而每一个这样的思想，这个系列都已经构建过：生日界、扇出、逻辑时钟、布隆过滤器、指派问题、控制回路、幂等性和 CRDT。每个设计都从一张餐巾纸开始，在一次模拟中结束。

dbb5018a5577.en: Every case follows the method of Part 48. <bookmark mark='a'/> Requirements first: what the system must do, and how well, in numbers. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the napkin: peak queries per second, storage and bandwidth. Then the interface and the data model, the calls and the keys. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then a high-level design built from the blocks, with one request traced through it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then the hard part, the one place where the design could fail, examined with numbers. And last, the trade-offs it forced, because there is never a design without them.
dbb5018a5577.zh: 每个案例都遵循第48部分的方法。<bookmark mark='a'/>需求在先：系统必须做什么，以及做得多好，用数字来表达。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是餐巾纸：高峰时的每秒查询数、存储量和带宽。然后是接口和数据模型，也就是调用和键。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后是用各个构件搭成的高层设计，并追踪一个请求穿过它的全过程。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后是难点，也就是设计可能失败的那一处，用数字来检验。最后是它被迫做出的权衡，因为从来没有不带权衡的设计。

820b0da91c87.en: This is Part 49 of Computer Science, Built. <bookmark mark='a'/> We will size a shortener's identifiers and choose a feed's fan-out on a power-law graph; order a chat's messages; keep a crawler polite; match riders to drivers as an assignment problem; adapt a video's bitrate as a control loop; keep a ledger that always sums to zero; make two editors converge; assemble a Dynamo-style store; and run the Job at a million books a day.
820b0da91c87.zh: 这是计算机科学，从零搭建，第49部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会为短网址服务的标识符确定长度，并在一张幂律图上为信息流选择扇出方式；给聊天的消息排序；让爬虫保持礼貌；把乘客与司机的匹配当作指派问题来解；把视频码率的自适应当作一个控制回路；维护一个总和永远为零的账本；让两个编辑器收敛；组装一个 Dynamo 式的存储；最后以每天100万本书的规模运行那项任务。

3d283b939c17.en: A URL shortener has two calls. <bookmark mark='a'/> One turns a long address into a short code; the other redirects from the code to the address. Links must last for years, and redirects must be fast. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the napkin, suppose a hundred million new links a month: about 39 a second. <bookmark mark='c'/> If each is followed a hundred times, that is about 3,858 redirects a second, three times that at the peak: overwhelmingly read-heavy. <bookmark mark='d'/> Five years make six billion links, and at five hundred bytes each, three terabytes, before replication.
3d283b939c17.zh: 短网址服务有两个调用。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个把长地址变成短码；另一个从短码重定向到地址。链接必须保存许多年，重定向必须很快。<bookmark mark='b'/>在餐巾纸上，假设每月有1亿个新链接：大约每秒39个。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果每个链接被点击100次，那就是大约每秒3858次重定向，高峰时是它的3倍：读远远多于写。<bookmark mark='d'/>5年就是60亿个链接，每个500字节，就是3太字节，这还没算复制。

ff18459f5035.en: How short can the code be? <bookmark mark='a'/> Letters in both cases and digits make sixty-two symbols, so N links need the logarithm of N to base sixty-two characters, rounded up. <bookmark mark='b'/> A million links fit in four characters, a billion in six, a trillion in seven. <bookmark mark='c'/> Converting a number is Part 4's positional notation: divide by sixty-two again and again, and the remainders, read upwards, are the digits of the trillionth link. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our six billion links need only six characters. The length was never the problem. Choosing each link's number is.
ff18459f5035.zh: 短码能有多短？<bookmark mark='a'/>大小写字母加上数字，一共62个符号，所以 N 个链接需要的字符数，是以62为底的 N 的对数，向上取整。<bookmark mark='b'/>100万个链接用4个字符就够了，10亿个用6个，1万亿个用7个。<bookmark mark='c'/>转换一个数，就是第4部分的位置记数法：反复除以62，余数从下往上读，就是第1万亿个链接的各位数字。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的60亿个链接只需要6个字符。长度从来不是问题。为每个链接选出它的编号才是。

a3fb44229f90.en: The design uses Part 48's blocks. <bookmark mark='a'/> A click reaches a load balancer, Maglev hashing, which spreads requests over stateless app servers. Behind them sit a cache, and a key-value store mapping codes to addresses, the Dynamo-style store of chapter ten. <bookmark mark='b'/> Follow a read. An app server asks the cache, where a hot code almost always is, and answers with a redirect; a record of the click goes onto a log, Part 46's streams, where a job counts clicks per link. <bookmark mark='c'/> A write is rarer. The app server takes the next number from a block of a million that a coordinator handed it, stores the code and address, and returns the code.
a3fb44229f90.zh: 这个设计使用第48部分的构件。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次点击到达一个负载均衡器，它用 Maglev 哈希把请求分散到无状态的应用服务器上。它们后面是一个缓存，以及一个把短码映射到地址的键值存储，也就是第十章的 Dynamo 式存储。<bookmark mark='b'/>跟着一次读走一遍。应用服务器询问缓存，热门的短码几乎总在那里，然后用一个重定向作答；一条点击记录被放进一个日志，也就是第46部分的流，那里有一个作业按链接统计点击数。<bookmark mark='c'/>写要少见得多。应用服务器从协调者分给它的一个100万编号的号段里取出下一个编号，保存短码和地址，然后返回短码。

d5e68b97005e.en: There are three ways to choose the number. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first hashes the address and keeps k characters. By Part 17's birthday bound, collisions come long before the space is full: with six characters, about nine among a million links, eighty-eight thousand among a hundred million. So every write must check the store and retry on a clash. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second is a counter, handed out in blocks: no checks, the shortest codes, but consecutive codes are guessable. <bookmark mark='c'/> The third is Part 48's Snowflake identifier: no coordination at all, but its sixty-four bits take 11 characters. <bookmark mark='d'/> A common choice is the counter, passed through a fixed scrambling bijection when codes must not be guessable.
d5e68b97005e.zh: 选择编号有三种办法。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一种对地址做哈希，保留 k 个字符。根据第17部分的生日界，远在空间被填满之前就会发生冲突：用6个字符时，100万个链接中大约有9次冲突，1亿个链接中有88000次。所以每次写都必须检查存储，遇到冲突就重试。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二种是计数器，按号段分发：不用检查，短码最短，但连续的短码可以被猜到。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三种是第48部分的 Snowflake 标识符：完全不需要协调，但它的64位要占11个字符。<bookmark mark='d'/>常见的选择是计数器，在短码不能被猜到时，再让它经过一个固定的置乱双射。

21a4d7d52320.en: The redirect itself is a choice, from Part 42's HTTP caching. <bookmark mark='a'/> A three-oh-one says the move is permanent. Browsers and edge caches remember it, and the second click never reaches us: cheap, but we lose the analytics and can never repoint the link. <bookmark mark='b'/> A three-oh-two says temporary, so every click comes back and is counted. <bookmark mark='c'/> Zipf's law makes that affordable: a few links get most clicks. On Part 48's Zipf traffic, a cache holding one percent of the items catches 43 percent of requests, and ten percent catches 65. <bookmark mark='d'/> The trade-off is our servers' load against the data and control we keep; a three-oh-one with a short cache lifetime sits in between.
21a4d7d52320.zh: 重定向本身也是一个选择，来自第42部分的 HTTP 缓存。<bookmark mark='a'/>301 表示这次搬迁是永久的。浏览器和边缘缓存会记住它，第二次点击根本到不了我们这里：很便宜，但我们失去了分析数据，也再也无法让这个链接改指别处。<bookmark mark='b'/>302 表示临时，所以每次点击都会回来，并被计数。<bookmark mark='c'/>齐普夫定律让这一点负担得起：少数链接获得了大部分点击。在第48部分的齐普夫流量上，一个容纳百分之1的项的缓存能接住百分之43的请求，容纳百分之10的能接住百分之65。<bookmark mark='d'/>权衡在于我们服务器的负载，与我们保留的数据和控制权之间；一个缓存存活时间很短的 301 介于两者之间。

1f400ccbd0e5.en: Chapter two. A news feed, and the question of fan-out.
1f400ccbd0e5.zh: 第二章：信息流，以及扇出的问题。

43ad67addc8e.en: A news feed shows each user the recent posts of everyone they follow. <bookmark mark='a'/> The data is a follower graph, and real follower graphs follow a power law: most accounts have a few dozen followers, and a handful have millions. <bookmark mark='b'/> Our instrument draws a synthetic graph of 100,000 users from such a law. The median account has 37 followers, but the mean is 138, pulled up by the giants, and the largest is followed by everyone. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each user posts half a time a day and opens the timeline twenty times: fifty thousand posts against two million reads. The question is when to do the work of putting those posts together.
43ad67addc8e.zh: 信息流向每个用户展示他所关注的每个人最近的帖子。<bookmark mark='a'/>数据是一张关注者图，而真实的关注者图服从幂律：大多数账号只有几十个关注者，而少数几个有数百万。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们的工具从这样一条定律中抽出一张有100000个用户的合成图。中位数账号有37个关注者，但平均值是138，被那些巨头拉高了，而最大的账号被所有人关注。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个用户每天发半条帖子，打开时间线20次：5万条帖子，对上200万次读取。问题是，什么时候去做把这些帖子汇集到一起的工作。

0cb1389a5535.en: There are two ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> Fan-out on write, or push: when someone posts, write the post into the timeline of every follower, so that reading a timeline is a single fetch. <bookmark mark='b'/> Fan-out on read, or pull: store each post once, with its author, and at every read gather the recent posts of everyone the reader follows. <bookmark mark='c'/> On our graph, push costs fifty thousand posts times 138 followers, about 6.9 million timeline writes a day. Pull costs two million reads times 138 followees, about 276 million fetches. <bookmark mark='d'/> Every follow is one follower and one followee, so the two averages are equal, and the ratio is just reads over posts: 40 times. Read-heavy, so push wins on total work.
0cb1389a5535.zh: 有两种办法。<bookmark mark='a'/>写时扇出，也就是推：有人发帖时，把帖子写进每个关注者的时间线，这样读一条时间线就是一次读取。<bookmark mark='b'/>读时扇出，也就是拉：每条帖子连同作者只存一次，每次读取时，再把读者关注的每个人最近的帖子收集起来。<bookmark mark='c'/>在我们的图上，推的代价是5万条帖子乘以138个关注者，每天大约6.9百万次时间线写入。拉的代价是200万次读取乘以138个关注对象，大约276百万次读取。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一条关注关系都是一个关注者对一个被关注者，所以两个平均值相等，而比值就是读取次数除以发帖数：40倍。读远多于写，所以按总工作量算，推胜出。

02492ade01e0.en: Push has a flaw, and it lives at the top of the power law. <bookmark mark='a'/> When the largest account posts, the system must write 99,999 timelines, a burst of work on the timeline store, and the last follower sees the post only when the last write lands. <bookmark mark='b'/> On a log scale the gap is plain: the median post fans out to 37 timelines, the mean to 138, and the largest to all of them. One such post costs as much as 2,703 ordinary ones. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the giants are few but heavy: the 119 accounts with at least ten thousand followers, about a tenth of a percent of users, receive 27 percent of all follows. Real networks have accounts with tens of millions of followers.
02492ade01e0.zh: 推有一个缺陷，它就住在幂律的顶端。<bookmark mark='a'/>当最大的账号发帖时，系统必须写99999条时间线，对时间线存储是一阵突发的工作，而最后一个关注者要等到最后一次写入落地，才能看到这条帖子。<bookmark mark='b'/>在对数刻度上，差距一目了然：中位数的帖子扇出到37条时间线，平均是138条，而最大的扇出到全部时间线。一条这样的帖子的代价，相当于2703条普通帖子。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且巨头虽少，分量却重：至少有1万个关注者的119个账号，大约占用户的千分之一，获得了全部关注的百分之27。真实的网络里有拥有几千万关注者的账号。

ce01c2646182.en: The cure is a hybrid. <bookmark mark='a'/> Push the posts of ordinary accounts, and pull the posts of accounts above a threshold at read time, merging them in. Our instrument counts both kinds of work for each threshold. <bookmark mark='b'/> Counted in operations, pure push is still cheapest: pulling the 119 giants multiplies the total about 12 fold, because pulls happen at every read. <bookmark mark='c'/> What the hybrid buys is the worst case. No post now fans out to more than 9,833 timelines, and the pulled posts are the same few hot items read by everyone, which a cache serves almost for free. <bookmark mark='d'/> Silberstein and colleagues made the choice per pair in 2010, comparing how often the author posts with how often the reader reads. The trade-off is total work against the tail.
ce01c2646182.zh: 解决办法是混合。<bookmark mark='a'/>普通账号的帖子用推，超过某个阈值的账号的帖子在读取时拉取，再合并进来。我们的工具为每个阈值统计两种工作。<bookmark mark='b'/>按操作次数算，纯推仍然最便宜：拉取那119个巨头，会让总量变成大约12倍，因为每次读取都要拉。<bookmark mark='c'/>混合方案买到的是最坏情况。现在没有哪条帖子会扇出到超过9833条时间线，而被拉取的帖子是人人都读的同样少数几个热门条目，缓存几乎可以免费地提供它们。<bookmark mark='d'/>Silberstein 和同事在2010年针对每一对用户做这个选择，比较作者发帖的频率与读者阅读的频率。权衡在于总工作量与尾部之间。

d9c662a6e725.en: Chapter three. A news feed, continued: ranking, and reading.
d9c662a6e725.zh: 第三章：信息流（续）：排序，以及读取。

9bb822a6039f.en: Chapter two decided how posts reach a timeline. Now read one. <bookmark mark='a'/> The reader's request reaches a stateless timeline service. <bookmark mark='b'/> It fetches the reader's timeline from a cache, a list of post identifiers that pushes have filled, and the latest posts of the few giants the reader follows, which are pulled. <bookmark mark='c'/> It merges the two lists, newest first, then hydrates them: looks each identifier up in the post store to get its text and author. A ranker orders them, and a page of twenty goes back. <bookmark mark='d'/> Timelines hold identifiers, not copies. Twitter described keeping about eight hundred per timeline in 2013; for our hundred thousand users, at eight bytes each, that is about 640 megabytes. And deleting a post is one write, not one per follower.
9bb822a6039f.zh: 第二章决定了帖子怎样到达一条时间线。现在来读一条。<bookmark mark='a'/>读者的请求到达一个无状态的时间线服务。<bookmark mark='b'/>它从缓存里取出读者的时间线，也就是由推送填充的一列帖子标识符，以及读者关注的少数几个巨头的最新帖子，这些是拉取来的。<bookmark mark='c'/>它把两个列表合并，最新的在前，然后补全（hydrate）它们：在帖子存储里查出每个标识符，得到它的文本和作者。一个排序器给它们排序，然后返回一页20条。<bookmark mark='d'/>时间线保存的是标识符，而不是副本。Twitter 在2013年说过，每条时间线保存大约800个；对我们的10万个用户，每个8字节，那大约是640兆字节。而且删除一条帖子只是一次写入，而不是每个关注者一次。

934e2cab0e53.en: The newest post is rarely the one a reader most wants. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are six candidates, newest first, with made-up numbers. <bookmark mark='b'/> Facebook's EdgeRank, described in 2010, scored each one as a product: the reader's affinity with the author, a weight for the kind of post, and a decay with age. <bookmark mark='c'/> Sorted by score, the order changes completely: the top is no longer the newest post, and a close friend's photo from sixteen hours ago outranks a stranger's from an hour ago. <bookmark mark='d'/> Modern feeds replace the hand-made product with learned models that predict each action a reader might take, Part 47's learning to rank, in two stages: a cheap one to choose candidates, and an expensive one to order the survivors.
934e2cab0e53.zh: 最新的帖子很少是读者最想看的那一条。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有6个候选，最新的在前，数字是编造的。<bookmark mark='b'/>Facebook 的 EdgeRank 在2010年公布，它把每一条的得分算成一个乘积：读者与作者的亲密度，帖子类型的权重，以及随时间的衰减。<bookmark mark='c'/>按得分排序，次序完全变了：排在最前面的不再是最新的帖子，一位好友16小时前的照片，排在一个陌生人1小时前的照片之前。<bookmark mark='d'/>现代的信息流用学习得到的模型取代了手工设计的乘积，这些模型预测读者可能采取的每一种行动，也就是第47部分的排序学习，分两个阶段：一个廉价的阶段挑选候选，一个昂贵的阶段给幸存者排序。

309b74cfe469.en: A reader scrolls, and the app asks for the next page. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a timeline, newest first, and the first page of four. <bookmark mark='b'/> While the reader looks at it, two new posts arrive at the top. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the next page is requested by offset, skip four and take four, the list has moved: the reader sees 2 posts again, and the database still walks past every skipped row, the problem of Part 43. <bookmark mark='d'/> A cursor instead says where the last page ended: everything older than this post. It is a position in the data, found with one index seek, and new posts at the top cannot disturb it. <bookmark mark='e'/> A ranked feed reorders between pages as well, so its cursor names a snapshot of the ranked list, cached for the session, and a position within it.
309b74cfe469.zh: 读者往下滚动，应用请求下一页。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一条时间线，最新的在前，以及第一页的4条。<bookmark mark='b'/>读者看着它的时候，顶部来了两条新帖子。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果下一页按偏移量请求，跳过4条再取4条，列表就已经移动了：读者会再次看到2条帖子，而数据库仍然要走过每一个被跳过的行，这是第43部分的问题。<bookmark mark='d'/>游标则说明上一页在哪里结束：比这条帖子更早的一切。它是数据中的一个位置，用一次索引查找就能找到，顶部的新帖子扰乱不了它。<bookmark mark='e'/>排序过的信息流在两页之间也会重新排序，所以它的游标指向排序列表的一个快照，在会话期间缓存起来，再加上快照中的一个位置。

cf2e3d2bc6f6.en: One more anomaly, from Part 39's replication. <bookmark mark='a'/> You post. The write goes to the leader, and replicas catch up a moment later. <bookmark mark='b'/> You open your timeline at once, the read lands on a replica that has not caught up, and your post is not there. So you post it again. <bookmark mark='c'/> There are three cures. Read from the leader for a minute after you write. Or carry the position of your last write, and have a replica answer only once it has applied that position, one of Part 39's session guarantees. Or let the app show your own post itself. <bookmark mark='d'/> Only the writer needs the guarantee. Everyone else can see the post a second late, and the feed stays cheap.
cf2e3d2bc6f6.zh: 还有一个异常，来自第39部分的复制。<bookmark mark='a'/>你发了一条帖子。写入去往领导者，副本稍后才追上。<bookmark mark='b'/>你立刻打开自己的时间线，这次读落在一个还没追上的副本上，你的帖子不在那里。于是你又发了一次。<bookmark mark='c'/>有三种解药。写入之后的一分钟里从领导者读。或者带上你最后一次写入的位置，让副本只有在应用到那个位置之后才作答，这是第39部分的会话保证之一。或者让应用自己显示你自己的帖子。<bookmark mark='d'/>只有写的人需要这个保证。其他人晚一秒看到帖子也无妨，信息流就能保持廉价。

fa5f0c9fed46.en: A chat service carries one-to-one and group messages. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each must arrive exactly once, in order, on every device, including phones that were off, with receipts and end-to-end encryption. <bookmark mark='b'/> Suppose a hundred million daily users sending forty messages each: about 46,000 a second, three times that at the peak. <bookmark mark='c'/> The bodies are small, about 400 gigabytes a day. <bookmark mark='d'/> The unusual number is connections: a waiting phone keeps one open, so fifty million are open at the peak. WhatsApp reported two million on one server in 2012, so twenty-five machines could in principle hold them; a real fleet is larger.
fa5f0c9fed46.zh: 聊天服务承载一对一消息和群组消息。<bookmark mark='a'/>每条消息都必须恰好到达一次，按顺序，到达每一台设备，包括那些关了机的手机，还要有回执和端到端加密。<bookmark mark='b'/>假设每天有1亿个用户，每人发40条消息：大约每秒46000条，高峰时是它的3倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>消息体很小，每天大约400吉字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>不寻常的数字是连接数：一部等待中的手机保持着一条打开的连接，所以高峰时有5000万条连接是打开的。WhatsApp 在2012年报告过一台服务器上有200万条连接，所以原则上25台机器就能容纳它们；真实的机群要更大。

24b5c02a396c.en: Here is the design. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each phone keeps a WebSocket open to a gateway: one long-lived connection on which the server can send without being asked. Gateways hold connections and nothing else, so they can be many and simple. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ana sends. Her gateway passes the message to the chat service, partitioned by conversation, which appends it to that conversation's log. <bookmark mark='c'/> A session registry, with short leases, says Ben's phone is on gateway three, and the message goes down that connection. <bookmark mark='d'/> If Ben's phone is asleep, the push service wakes it through the phone maker's notification system, and the phone connects and fetches what it missed.
24b5c02a396c.zh: 这是设计。<bookmark mark='a'/>每部手机都向一个网关保持一条打开的 WebSocket：一条长期存在的连接，服务器可以在上面主动发送，不必等被问。网关只持有连接，别的什么都不做，所以它们可以数量众多而且简单。<bookmark mark='b'/>Ana 发送一条消息。她的网关把消息交给按对话分区的聊天服务，后者把它追加到这个对话的日志里。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个带短租约的会话注册表说明，Ben 的手机在3号网关上，于是消息顺着那条连接发下去。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果 Ben 的手机在休眠，推送服务就通过手机厂商的通知系统唤醒它，手机连上来，取回它错过的消息。

affbf8e6f610.en: The hard part is order. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ben asks, dinner at eight? Ana reads it and answers yes. <bookmark mark='b'/> But her phone's clock runs three seconds slow, so her answer is stamped earlier than his question. <bookmark mark='c'/> Sorted by the phones' clocks, the answer comes first. Server clocks differ too, as Part 38 showed: unsynchronised clocks cannot order events reliably. <bookmark mark='d'/> The fix is a sequence number. Each conversation has one owner, its partition's leader, which numbers messages as they arrive. Ana answered after seeing forty-one, so her answer gets a larger number. The order holds within a conversation only, which is all a reader sees, and a retried send carries the same client identifier, Part 43's idempotency key, and keeps its number.
affbf8e6f610.zh: 难点在于顺序。<bookmark mark='a'/>Ben 问：8点吃晚饭？Ana 读到了，回答：好。<bookmark mark='b'/>但她手机的时钟慢了3秒，所以她的回答被盖上的时间戳比他的问题还早。<bookmark mark='c'/>按手机的时钟排序，回答就排到了前面。服务器的时钟也各不相同，正如第38部分所展示的：不同步的时钟无法可靠地给事件排序。<bookmark mark='d'/>修正办法是序列号。每个对话有一个所有者，也就是它所在分区的领导者，它在消息到达时给它们编号。Ana 是在看到41号之后回答的，所以她的回答得到一个更大的编号。这个顺序只在一个对话之内成立，而这正是读者看到的全部；一次重试的发送带着同一个客户端标识符，也就是第43部分的幂等键，并保留它的编号。

22fa4209a325.en: Sequence numbers also give receipts and offline sync almost for free. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each conversation's log is numbered. Ben's phone acknowledges what it has received, up to forty-four: that is the second tick, delivered. <bookmark mark='b'/> When Ben has looked, his phone reports read up to forty-two. Each receipt is a watermark, one number per member and device, not a record per message. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now Ben's phone is switched off, and three more messages arrive. <bookmark mark='d'/> When it reconnects it asks for everything after forty-four, and gets exactly the three it missed. And a phone that holds forty-four and suddenly receives forty-six knows that forty-five is missing, and asks for it.
22fa4209a325.zh: 序列号还几乎免费地带来了回执和离线同步。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个对话的日志都是编了号的。Ben 的手机确认它已经收到的部分，直到44号：这就是第二个勾，已送达。<bookmark mark='b'/>Ben 看过之后，他的手机报告已读到42号。每个回执都是一条水位线，每个成员、每台设备一个数，而不是每条消息一条记录。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在 Ben 的手机关机了，又来了3条消息。<bookmark mark='d'/>它重新连接时，请求44号之后的所有消息，恰好得到它错过的那3条。而一部持有44号、却突然收到46号的手机，就知道45号丢了，并去请求它。

e276e4335ef9.en: Two last pieces. <bookmark mark='a'/> A group message is stored once and fanned out to every member, the push of chapter two, with pulls for very large groups. <bookmark mark='b'/> With end-to-end encryption the server only ever relays ciphertext. Between two devices, Signal's double ratchet, published by Trevor Perrin and Moxie Marlinspike in 2016, derives each message's key by hashing the previous chain key, Part 29, and deletes it after use, so a stolen phone cannot read old messages. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each reply also mixes in a fresh Diffie-Hellman exchange, Part 30, which locks a thief out of new ones. <bookmark mark='d'/> WhatsApp's groups use sender keys, distributed pairwise once, so a message is encrypted once. <bookmark mark='e'/> The price: the server cannot search or filter content, and every extra device is another recipient.
e276e4335ef9.zh: 最后两部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>一条群组消息只存一次，然后扇出到每个成员，也就是第二章的推，而对非常大的群组则用拉。<bookmark mark='b'/>有了端到端加密，服务器只转发密文。在两台设备之间，Signal 的双棘轮算法，由 Trevor Perrin 和 Moxie Marlinspike 在2016年发布，通过对上一个链密钥求哈希来推导每条消息的密钥，这是第29部分的内容，并在用过之后删除它，所以一部被偷的手机读不了旧消息。<bookmark mark='c'/>每次回复还会混入一次新的 Diffie-Hellman 交换，这是第30部分的内容，它把窃贼挡在新消息之外。<bookmark mark='d'/>WhatsApp 的群组使用发送者密钥，两两分发一次，这样一条消息只加密一次。<bookmark mark='e'/>代价是：服务器无法搜索或过滤内容，而每多一台设备，就多一个接收者。

f64ac3420679.en: Requirements first. A search engine, like the one of Part 47, wants a billion pages fetched every month, politely, and never the same page twice. <bookmark mark='a'/> A billion pages in thirty days is about three hundred and eighty-six pages a second. <bookmark mark='b'/> If a fetch takes half a second, about a hundred and ninety-three are in flight at once; at a hundred kilobytes a page, that is about a third of a gigabit a second, and one machine could carry it. <bookmark mark='c'/> What makes the crawler hard is manners. A polite crawler asks any one host for at most one page a second, so to keep its rate it must be busy with at least three hundred and eighty-six different hosts at once. And it must remember every URL it has seen: a billion of them.
f64ac3420679.zh: 需求在先。一个搜索引擎，就像第47部分的那个，希望每个月抓取10亿个网页，要有礼貌，并且同一个网页绝不抓两次。<bookmark mark='a'/>30天10亿个网页，大约是每秒386个网页。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果一次抓取需要半秒，同时大约有193个在进行中；每个网页100千字节，那大约是每秒三分之一吉比特，一台机器就能承担。<bookmark mark='c'/>让爬虫变难的是礼貌。一个有礼貌的爬虫，对任何一个主机每秒至多请求一个网页，所以为了保持它的速率，它必须同时忙于至少386个不同的主机。而且它必须记住它见过的每个 URL：10亿个。

93c66c792fff.en: The design is a loop. <bookmark mark='a'/> Seed URLs enter the frontier, the list of pages still to fetch. A fetcher takes one, looks up its host name and downloads the page, and the parser stores it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Name lookups would dominate if done naively, so every fetcher keeps a DNS cache, Part 37's resolver; Mercator, the crawler Allan Heydon and Marc Najork described in 1999, found lookups slow enough to write its own resolver. <bookmark mark='c'/> The parser also extracts the page's links. Each is checked against the set of URLs already seen, and only new ones go back to the frontier. <bookmark mark='d'/> Across machines the work is split by a hash of the host name, so everything about one host lives on one machine, and a link to another host is forwarded to the machine that owns it.
93c66c792fff.zh: 这个设计是一个循环。<bookmark mark='a'/>种子 URL 进入待抓取队列（frontier），也就是仍待抓取的网页列表。抓取器取出一个，查找它的主机名并下载网页，解析器把它存起来。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果做得天真，名字查找会占主导，所以每个抓取器都保留一个 DNS 缓存，也就是第37部分的解析器；Mercator，Allan Heydon 和 Marc Najork 在1999年描述的那个爬虫，发现查找慢到值得自己写一个解析器。<bookmark mark='c'/>解析器还提取网页的链接。每个链接都与已见过的 URL 集合比对，只有新的才回到待抓取队列。<bookmark mark='d'/>在多台机器之间，工作按主机名的哈希来拆分，所以关于一个主机的一切都在一台机器上，而指向另一个主机的链接会被转发给拥有它的那台机器。

aa1f65d39c6c.en: The frontier is the heart of a crawler, and Mercator's design of it is still the textbook one. <bookmark mark='a'/> New URLs are first sorted by priority, by importance or how often a page changes, into a few front queues. <bookmark mark='b'/> Behind them sit back queues, one for each host, each holding only that host's URLs. <bookmark mark='c'/> A heap, the priority queue of Part 17, keyed by the earliest time each host may be visited again, decides what is fetched next. Pop the host whose time has come, fetch the URL at the head of its queue, and push the host back with a new time. <bookmark mark='d'/> The new time is the politeness rule: here one request a second; a common heuristic waits several times as long as the last fetch took, so a struggling server is asked less often.
aa1f65d39c6c.zh: 待抓取队列是爬虫的心脏，而 Mercator 对它的设计至今仍是教科书式的。<bookmark mark='a'/>新的 URL 先按优先级，也就是按重要性或网页变化的频率，分进几个前端队列。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们后面是后端队列，每个主机一个，每个只放那个主机的 URL。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个堆，也就是第17部分的优先队列，以每个主机最早可以再次访问的时间为键，决定下一个抓取什么。弹出时间已到的主机，抓取它队列头部的 URL，再带着一个新时间把主机推回去。<bookmark mark='d'/>新时间就是礼貌规则：这里是每秒一个请求；一种常见的经验法则是等待上一次抓取所用时间的若干倍，这样一台吃力的服务器被请求的次数就会更少。

91ace282cdf7.en: And the crawler must not fetch a page twice. <bookmark mark='a'/> The seen set is a Bloom filter, from Part 20: each URL sets a few bits, chosen by independent hashes. <bookmark mark='b'/> A new URL whose bits are all set is reported as seen, sometimes wrongly: these three were set by two other URLs. <bookmark mark='c'/> We measured our filter: two hundred thousand URLs at nine point six bits each and seven hashes gave one point zero zero five percent false positives, against zero point nine nine seven from the formula. <bookmark mark='d'/> For a billion URLs that is one point two gigabytes, in memory. A false positive costs a page never fetched; there are no false negatives, so nothing is fetched twice. <bookmark mark='e'/> Different URLs often serve the same text, so crawlers also fingerprint content. With Moses Charikar's SimHash, similar pages get fingerprints a few bits apart, and Gurmeet Manku and colleagues at Google reported in 2007 that sixty-four bits, at most three differing, worked across eight billion pages.
91ace282cdf7.zh: 而且爬虫不能把一个网页抓两次。<bookmark mark='a'/>已见集合是一个布隆过滤器，来自第20部分：每个 URL 设置几个位，由相互独立的哈希选出。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个新 URL，如果它的位全都已被设置，就被报告为见过，有时是错的：这3个位是被另外两个 URL 设置的。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们测量了自己的过滤器：20万个 URL，每个9.6位，7个哈希，得到百分之1.005的假阳性，而公式给出的是百分之0.997。<bookmark mark='d'/>对10亿个 URL，那是1.2吉字节，放在内存里。一次假阳性的代价是一个网页永远不会被抓取；不存在假阴性，所以没有什么会被抓两次。<bookmark mark='e'/>不同的 URL 常常提供同样的文本，所以爬虫还会给内容算指纹。用 Moses Charikar 的 SimHash，相似的网页得到只相差几位的指纹，而 Google 的 Gurmeet Manku 和同事在2007年报告说，64位、至多3位不同，在80亿个网页上都行之有效。

9aed73a31694.en: A dispatcher must know where every driver is, all the time. <bookmark mark='a'/> Say a million drivers are online, each phone reporting its position every four seconds: that is two hundred and fifty thousand writes a second, each one replacing the last. <bookmark mark='b'/> So the hot store keeps only each driver's latest position, in memory, indexed by map cell, and lets stale entries expire; the history goes to a log, as in Part 46. <bookmark mark='c'/> The cells are hexagons, as in Uber's H3 index from Part 48. A hexagon's six neighbours are all the same distance away, so the drivers near a rider are simply those in the rider's cell and the ring around it.
9aed73a31694.zh: 派单系统必须时刻知道每个司机在哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设有100万个司机在线，每部手机每4秒报告一次位置：那就是每秒25万次写入，每一次都替换上一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以热存储只保存每个司机的最新位置，放在内存里，按地图格子建索引，并让过时的条目过期；历史数据进入一个日志，就像第46部分那样。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些格子是六边形，就像第48部分里 Uber 的 H3 索引。一个六边形的6个邻居全都一样远，所以乘客附近的司机，就是乘客所在的格子以及它周围那一圈里的司机。

3039b13181e3.en: Here is the whole service. <bookmark mark='a'/> Phones keep a connection open to a gateway, the same connection servers as the chat of Chapter 4. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the write path, drivers' pings flow through a location service that overwrites each driver's entry in the geo index. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the read path, a rider's request reaches dispatch, which asks the index for the drivers in the nearby cells, ranks them by driving time from the ETA service, and sends the chosen driver an offer over the connection that driver already has open. If the driver declines or does not answer within a few seconds, the offer moves to the next.
3039b13181e3.zh: 这是整个服务。<bookmark mark='a'/>手机向一个网关保持一条打开的连接，和第四章聊天服务用的是同一种连接服务器。<bookmark mark='b'/>在写路径上，司机上报的位置流经一个位置服务，它覆盖地理索引中每个司机的条目。<bookmark mark='c'/>在读路径上，乘客的请求到达派单服务，它向索引询问附近格子里的司机，按 ETA 服务给出的驾车时间给他们排序，然后通过被选中的司机已经打开的那条连接，向他发出一个派单邀约。如果司机拒绝了，或者几秒钟之内没有回应，邀约就转给下一个。

f003e5a75858.en: The hard idea: which driver takes which rider? <bookmark mark='a'/> The obvious rule is greedy: as each request arrives, give it the nearest free driver. Here rider A arrives first and takes the only driver near B, so B gets the far one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Collect both requests and match them together, and the total is smaller. Matching a batch is the assignment problem of Part 18, solved exactly; Harold Kuhn's Hungarian algorithm of 1955 was the first, and our solver reaches the same optimum by a faster modern method. <bookmark mark='c'/> We simulated it: sixty riders and seventy drivers scattered over a ten-kilometre city, two hundred times. Greedy's mean pickup was one point one seven kilometres; batched, zero point nine six. <bookmark mark='d'/> The worst pickup in each round fell much more, from four point eight to three point zero, because greedy's last riders get whatever is left. The price is a batching window of a few seconds.
f003e5a75858.zh: 难点在于：哪个司机接哪位乘客？<bookmark mark='a'/>显而易见的规则是贪心：每个请求到达时，就把最近的空闲司机给它。这里乘客 A 先到，拿走了 B 附近唯一的司机，于是 B 只能得到远处那个。<bookmark mark='b'/>把两个请求收集起来一起匹配，总距离就更小。匹配一批请求，就是第18部分的指派问题，可以精确求解；哈罗德·库恩（Harold Kuhn）1955年的匈牙利算法是第一个解法，而我们的求解器用一种更快的现代方法得到同样的最优解。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们做了模拟：60位乘客和70个司机散布在一座10公里宽的城市里，重复200次。贪心的平均接驾距离是1.17公里；分批的是0.96公里。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一轮中最差的接驾距离下降得多得多，从4.8公里降到3.0公里，因为在贪心之下，最后的乘客只能拿到剩下的司机。代价是一个几秒钟的分批窗口。

7c47729cceec.en: To choose among drivers, dispatch needs driving times, thousands a second. <bookmark mark='a'/> Contraction hierarchies, from Robert Geisberger and colleagues in 2008, prepare the road graph in advance. Remove the least important junction; wherever the shortest path between two of its neighbours ran through it, add a shortcut of the same length. <bookmark mark='b'/> Repeat for every junction, in order of importance, and the graph gains a hierarchy of shortcuts. <bookmark mark='c'/> A query then runs Dijkstra's search from both ends, each only climbing upward, and the two meet near the top. As Part 18 measured, such a query settles a small fraction of the junctions that plain Dijkstra would.
7c47729cceec.zh: 为了在司机之间做选择，派单需要驾车时间，每秒几千个。<bookmark mark='a'/>收缩层级（contraction hierarchies），由 Robert Geisberger 和同事在2008年提出，预先处理道路图。去掉最不重要的路口；凡是它的两个邻居之间的最短路径经过它的地方，就加一条同样长度的捷径。<bookmark mark='b'/>按重要性的顺序对每个路口重复这一步，图就获得了一个由捷径组成的层级。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后一次查询从两端运行迪杰斯特拉搜索，每一端都只往上爬，两者在顶部附近相遇。正如第18部分所测量的，这样一次查询确定的路口，只占普通迪杰斯特拉算法所确定的一小部分。

267eb169bdb6.en: The last piece is economic. <bookmark mark='a'/> In each cell, every minute or two, the system compares open requests with free drivers. The price settles where supply and demand cross. <bookmark mark='b'/> When a concert ends, demand jumps, and at the old price there are not enough drivers. A higher price clears the market: it draws drivers in and persuades some riders to wait. <bookmark mark='c'/> Jonathan Hall, Cory Kendrick and Chris Nosko compared, in 2015, a night when Uber's surge pricing worked with one when it briefly failed: without it, fewer requests were completed and waits grew. <bookmark mark='d'/> The trade-off here is not technical: efficiency against fairness, and so surge is capped in emergencies.
267eb169bdb6.zh: 最后一部分是经济上的。<bookmark mark='a'/>在每个格子里，每隔一两分钟，系统比较未完成的请求和空闲的司机。价格落在供给与需求相交的地方。<bookmark mark='b'/>一场音乐会结束时，需求猛增，而按原来的价格，司机不够。更高的价格让市场出清：它把司机吸引过来，并说服一些乘客等一等。<bookmark mark='c'/>Jonathan Hall、Cory Kendrick 和 Chris Nosko 在2015年比较了两个夜晚：一晚 Uber 的动态加价正常运作，另一晚它短暂失灵；没有它，完成的请求更少，等待更长。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里的权衡不是技术上的：效率对公平，所以在紧急情况下，动态加价会被设上限。

4dfc8ac0b51d.en: A video platform must start quickly, never stall, and look as good as each viewer's connection allows. <bookmark mark='a'/> So every upload is encoded several times, into a ladder of qualities, here six from zero point three to four point three megabits a second, and each version is cut into segments two seconds long. <bookmark mark='b'/> A manifest lists them: Apple's HTTP Live Streaming, from 2009, and the MPEG-DASH standard of 2012 work this way. Every segment is an ordinary file fetched over HTTP, so the caches of Part 42 serve video as they serve anything else. <bookmark mark='c'/> The player chooses a rung for every segment; here are the choices our buffer-based player made. <bookmark mark='d'/> The napkin: an hour at the top rung is about one point nine gigabytes to send, and storing every rung costs about five gigabytes per hour of video.
4dfc8ac0b51d.zh: 视频平台必须启动得快，从不卡顿，并且在每个观众的网络连接允许的范围内尽可能好看。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以每个上传的视频都要编码好几次，形成一个质量阶梯，这里是6档，从每秒0.3兆比特到4.3兆比特，而每个版本都被切成2秒长的分段。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个清单文件把它们列出来：Apple 2009年的 HTTP Live Streaming 和2012年的 MPEG-DASH 标准都是这样工作的。每个分段都是一个通过 HTTP 获取的普通文件，所以第42部分的缓存提供视频，就像提供其他任何东西一样。<bookmark mark='c'/>播放器为每个分段选择一档；这里是我们基于缓冲区的播放器做出的选择。<bookmark mark='d'/>餐巾纸：最高一档的一小时视频，大约要发送1.9吉字节，而存储所有档位，每小时视频大约要花5吉字节。

7feda2d80603.en: The design follows. <bookmark mark='a'/> An upload goes into a queue, and encoders work through it. Because segments are independent, one title is encoded by many machines at once, a batch job of the kind Part 45 rents by the minute. <bookmark mark='b'/> The finished segments sit in a blob store, the origin, and are served through the content delivery network of Part 42. <bookmark mark='c'/> Popularity follows a Zipf law, as Part 37 found for words: a few titles take most of the views, so the edges hold the head, and a request for something in the long tail travels back to the origin. Netflix goes further: its Open Connect caches sit inside internet providers' own networks, filled overnight with what is likely to be watched the next day.
7feda2d80603.zh: 设计随之而来。<bookmark mark='a'/>上传的视频进入一个队列，由编码器逐个处理。因为分段是彼此独立的，一部作品可以同时由许多台机器编码，这是第45部分那种按分钟租用的批处理作业。<bookmark mark='b'/>编码完成的分段放在一个大对象存储里，也就是源站，并通过第42部分的内容分发网络提供出去。<bookmark mark='c'/>热度服从齐普夫定律，正如第37部分在词语上发现的那样：少数作品占去了大部分观看，所以边缘保存头部，而对长尾中某个东西的请求，要一路回到源站。Netflix 走得更远：它的 Open Connect 缓存就放在互联网服务提供商自己的网络里，在夜间填入第二天可能被观看的内容。

63d9c6d58735.en: Choosing the rung is a control problem, the same shape as Part 37's congestion control: act, observe, adjust. <bookmark mark='a'/> The grey line is the bandwidth of one simulated connection, wandering between good, fair and poor. The obvious controller is rate-based: estimate the throughput of recent downloads and pick the highest rung beneath it. But estimates are noisy, and a wrong guess drains the buffer. <bookmark mark='b'/> Te-Yuan Huang and colleagues at Netflix argued in 2014 for choosing from the buffer alone: the lowest rung while the buffer is below a reservoir, the highest once it passes a cushion, and a straight line between. Here is that player: its quality follows its buffer. <bookmark mark='c'/> Xiaoqi Yin and colleagues, in 2015, used model predictive control: predict the bandwidth, try each bitrate held over the next five segments, choosing the one that maximizes quality minus penalties for stalls and switches, take the first step, and plan again.
63d9c6d58735.zh: 选择档位是一个控制问题，和第37部分的拥塞控制形状相同：行动，观察，调整。<bookmark mark='a'/>灰线是一条模拟连接的带宽，在好、中、差之间游移。显而易见的控制器是基于速率的：估计最近几次下载的吞吐量，选出低于它的最高一档。但估计有噪声，一次错误的猜测就会耗干缓冲区。<bookmark mark='b'/>Netflix 的 Te-Yuan Huang 和同事在2014年主张只根据缓冲区来选择：缓冲区低于储备区时用最低档，一旦超过缓冲垫就用最高档，两者之间是一条直线。这就是那个播放器：它的质量跟着它的缓冲区走。<bookmark mark='c'/>Xiaoqi Yin 和同事在2015年使用了模型预测控制：预测带宽，试遍在接下来5个分段上保持不变的每一种码率，选出使质量减去卡顿和切换惩罚之后最大的那一种，走出第一步，然后重新规划。

cfd6d21e821e.en: We ran all three on five synthetic ten-minute traces. <bookmark mark='a'/> Mean quality: rate-based two point three three megabits a second, buffer-based two point six six, MPC two point seven nine. <bookmark mark='b'/> Stalls: the buffer-based player never stalled at all. The rate-based player stalled for about three seconds, and our MPC for about five: it bought the best picture by trusting its forecast and keeping less in reserve, so sudden drops caught it. Yin and colleagues, with a better predictor, found MPC ahead. <bookmark mark='c'/> All three switched quality between fifty and sixty-five times. <bookmark mark='d'/> Which matters most? Florin Dobrian and colleagues found in 2011 that, of the quality measures they studied, time spent rebuffering hurt viewers' engagement most. How to weigh picture against stalls is a product decision, written into the controller's objective.
cfd6d21e821e.zh: 我们在5条合成的10分钟轨迹上运行了全部三种。<bookmark mark='a'/>平均质量：基于速率的是每秒2.33兆比特，基于缓冲区的是2.66，MPC 是2.79。<bookmark mark='b'/>卡顿：基于缓冲区的播放器一次都没有卡顿。基于速率的播放器卡顿了大约3秒，我们的 MPC 大约5秒：它靠信任自己的预测、少留储备，换来了最好的画面，于是突然的下降让它措手不及。Yin 和同事用了一个更好的预测器，发现 MPC 领先。<bookmark mark='c'/>三者切换质量的次数都在50到65次之间。<bookmark mark='d'/>哪一项最重要？Florin Dobrian 和同事在2011年发现，在他们研究的各种质量指标中，花在重新缓冲上的时间对观众参与度的伤害最大。画面与卡顿之间如何权衡，是一个产品决策，写进控制器的目标函数里。

7fbcca4714ad.en: A payment system is first of all a ledger, kept the way accountants have kept books for five hundred years. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every payment is a journal entry with several lines: fifty dollars leave the customer, forty-eight fifty reach the merchant, and a dollar fifty goes to fees. The lines sum to zero. Amounts are whole numbers of cents, never floating point, as Part 4 warned. <bookmark mark='b'/> A second payment, the same way. <bookmark mark='c'/> Because every entry sums to zero, the whole ledger does, by the induction of Part 2: money is moved, never made or lost. <bookmark mark='d'/> Entries are only ever appended. A mistake is fixed by a new entry that reverses it, so the ledger is its own audit trail.
7fbcca4714ad.zh: 支付系统首先是一个账本，按照会计师们500年来记账的方式来记。<bookmark mark='a'/>每笔支付都是一条有几行的日记账分录：50美元离开顾客，48.50美元到达商家，1.50美元作为手续费。这些行加起来等于零。金额是以分为单位的整数，绝不用浮点数，正如第4部分所警告的。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二笔支付，也一样。<bookmark mark='c'/>因为每条分录加起来都是零，整个账本也是，这是第2部分的归纳法：钱只被转移，从不被创造或丢失。<bookmark mark='d'/>分录只会被追加。错误靠一条把它冲销的新分录来修正，所以账本就是它自己的审计轨迹。

375b7ac0a9b7.en: The design. <bookmark mark='a'/> A client asks the payments API to charge fifty dollars. The API writes the ledger entry to a single-leader database, and an outbox, Part 43's pattern, carries the request to the card processor. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the reply is lost. The client cannot know whether the charge happened, so it must retry, and a naive server would charge twice. <bookmark mark='c'/> The cure is an idempotency key. The client chooses one key per payment and sends it with every attempt. The server records the key and its result in the same transaction as the ledger entry, so a repeat finds the key and returns the stored reply instead of charging again. <bookmark mark='d'/> Pat Helland put it simply in 2012: in a world of retries, every request should be idempotent.
375b7ac0a9b7.zh: 设计。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个客户端请求支付 API 扣款50美元。API 把账本分录写进一个单领导者数据库，再由一个发件箱（outbox），也就是第43部分的模式，把请求送到银行卡处理方。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后回复丢了。客户端无法知道扣款是否发生了，所以它必须重试，而一个天真的服务器会扣两次款。<bookmark mark='c'/>解药是幂等键。客户端为每笔支付选一个键，并在每次尝试时都带上它。服务器在与账本分录相同的事务里记录这个键及其结果，所以一次重复的请求会找到这个键，返回存下的回复，而不是再扣一次款。<bookmark mark='d'/>Pat Helland 在2012年说得很简单：在一个充满重试的世界里，每个请求都应该是幂等的。

21c5aaf8ea22.en: We simulated it with our ledger instrument: five thousand payments of random amounts, where some attempts time out and are retried and some are declined. <bookmark mark='a'/> Without keys, six thousand two hundred and nine entries were posted, and one thousand three hundred and ninety payments, nearly three in ten, were charged twice. <bookmark mark='b'/> With keys, no payment was charged twice. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now look at the invariant. Both ledgers sum to exactly zero. Every double charge was itself a perfectly balanced entry, so the books balance and are still wrong. <bookmark mark='d'/> Balance is one invariant; at most one entry per payment is another, and only the key table enforces it.
21c5aaf8ea22.zh: 我们用自己的账本工具做了模拟：5000笔随机金额的支付，其中有些尝试超时并被重试，有些被拒绝。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有键时，记入了6209条分录，有1390笔支付，将近十分之三，被扣了两次款。<bookmark mark='b'/>有了键，没有一笔支付被扣两次。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在看不变量。两个账本加起来都恰好是零。每一次重复扣款本身都是一条完全平衡的分录，所以账目是平的，却仍然是错的。<bookmark mark='d'/>平衡是一个不变量；每笔支付至多一条分录是另一个，而只有键表能强制保证它。

3f31e257858e.en: A card payment is a state machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> It is created; the card's bank authorizes it, placing a hold; the merchant captures it, and money moves; days later it settles, and the cash arrives. Along the way it can be declined, voided before capture, or refunded after. <bookmark mark='b'/> Transitions only go forward, and each is a compare-and-set on the current state, so a duplicate capture finds the payment already captured and does nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> The state change, its ledger lines and the outbox message are written in one database transaction, from Part 35, so none is ever seen without the others.
3f31e257858e.zh: 一笔银行卡支付是一个状态机。<bookmark mark='a'/>它被创建；发卡银行对它授权，冻结相应的额度；商家请款，钱开始流动；几天之后它完成结算，现金到账。一路上，它可能被拒绝，在请款之前被撤销，或者在请款之后被退款。<bookmark mark='b'/>状态转移只会向前，而且每一次都是对当前状态的一次比较并设置（compare-and-set），所以一次重复的请款会发现支付已经被请款，于是什么也不做。<bookmark mark='c'/>状态变化、它的账本行和发件箱消息，在第35部分的一个数据库事务里写入，所以永远不会只看到其中一个而看不到其他。

0d8c845793ca.en: Two more duties remain. <bookmark mark='a'/> The ledger is only our account of events; the processor and the banks keep theirs. Every day, each of our entries is matched against the processor's settlement file. Most agree. <bookmark mark='b'/> Some do not: an amount that differs, an entry one side has and the other lacks. These go to a queue for people. <bookmark mark='c'/> The last trade-off is the one Part 39 named. During a network partition, a ledger refuses to write rather than let two replicas disagree about a balance; it chooses consistency over availability. <bookmark mark='d'/> Availability is won back at the edge: accept the request, answer pending, and let the outbox finish the work when the ledger can.
0d8c845793ca.zh: 还剩两项职责。<bookmark mark='a'/>账本只是我们对事件的记录；处理方和银行各有各的记录。每天，我们的每条分录都要与处理方的结算文件逐一核对。大多数是一致的。<bookmark mark='b'/>有些不一致：金额不同，或者一方有、另一方没有的分录。这些进入一个队列，交给人来处理。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后一个权衡，是第39部分命名过的那个。在网络分区期间，账本宁可拒绝写入，也不让两个副本对一个余额产生分歧；它选择一致性而不是可用性。<bookmark mark='d'/>可用性在边缘赢回来：接受请求，回答“处理中”，等账本可以写的时候，再让发件箱完成工作。

bdba15fe60a3.en: A collaborative editor lets several people type into one document at once. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every keystroke must appear at once on the typist's own screen; nobody waits for a server. <bookmark mark='b'/> When the typing stops, every copy must hold the same text: convergence. <bookmark mark='c'/> And each edit should land where its author meant it, whatever others typed meanwhile. <bookmark mark='d'/> The design is small. Editors hold WebSocket connections to a collaboration server, which relays each operation and appends it to a log, compacted into snapshots. <bookmark mark='e'/> The load is tiny, perhaps fifty operations a second for a busy document. The hard part is order.
bdba15fe60a3.zh: 协同编辑器让几个人同时在一份文档里打字。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一次按键都必须立刻出现在打字者自己的屏幕上；没有人等待服务器。<bookmark mark='b'/>打字停下时，每一份副本都必须保存同样的文本：收敛。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且每次编辑都应该落在作者想要的位置，不管其他人在此期间输入了什么。<bookmark mark='d'/>这个设计很小。编辑器与一个协作服务器保持 WebSocket 连接，服务器转发每一个操作，并把它追加到一个日志里，日志再压缩成快照。<bookmark mark='e'/>负载很小，一份繁忙的文档也许每秒50个操作。难点在于顺序。

46deb1ab5494.en: Here is why order is hard. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two people share the text, the cat sat. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the same moment, A inserts the letter z at position one, and B appends an x at position eleven, the end. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then each applies the other's operation as sent. At B, that is still right. But at A, position eleven no longer means the end: the z pushed everything one place right, so the x lands between the a and the t. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two copies, two texts. A position only means something in the state it was made in.
46deb1ab5494.zh: 这就是为什么顺序很难。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个人共享文本 the cat sat。<bookmark mark='b'/>在同一时刻，A 在位置1插入字母 z，B 在位置11，也就是末尾，追加一个 x。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后各自按原样应用对方的操作。在 B 那里，这仍然是对的。但在 A 那里，位置11不再表示末尾：z 把一切都往右推了一位，所以 x 落在了 a 和 t 之间。<bookmark mark='d'/>两份副本，两种文本。一个位置只在它被创建时的那个状态里才有意义。

24b679b6051e.en: Operational transformation, from Clarence Ellis and Simon Gibbs in 1989, repairs an operation before applying it. <bookmark mark='a'/> A transforms B's insert at eleven against its own concurrent insert at one. That came earlier in the text, so B's position shifts right, to twelve. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now both copies agree. <bookmark mark='c'/> The rules are few: an insert before you pushes you right, a delete before you pulls you left, and a tie is settled by a fixed priority between sites. <bookmark mark='d'/> Over five thousand random pairs of concurrent edits, transformation converged every time; applied as sent, only about six in a hundred did. <bookmark mark='e'/> With many sites the original algorithm was later found to diverge, so Jupiter, in 1995, and later Google Docs route every operation through one server, which fixes a single order.
24b679b6051e.zh: 操作转换，由 Clarence Ellis 和 Simon Gibbs 在1989年提出，在应用一个操作之前先修正它。<bookmark mark='a'/>A 把 B 在位置11的插入，针对它自己在位置1的并发插入做转换。那个插入在文本中更靠前，所以 B 的位置右移到12。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在两份副本一致了。<bookmark mark='c'/>规则很少：在你之前的插入把你往右推，在你之前的删除把你往左拉，而平局由站点之间的固定优先级来裁决。<bookmark mark='d'/>在5000对随机的并发编辑上，转换每一次都收敛了；按原样应用，只有大约百分之6收敛。<bookmark mark='e'/>后来发现，在站点很多时，原来的算法会发散，所以1995年的 Jupiter，以及后来的 Google Docs，让每个操作都经过一台服务器，由它确定唯一的顺序。

1b857a82dd25.en: The other answer is to stop using positions. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a sequence CRDT, here the replicated growable array of Roh and colleagues, 2011, every character gets a permanent name: a counter, and the replica that made it. <bookmark mark='b'/> An insert names the character it goes after. Here two people type after the t at once. <bookmark mark='c'/> A fixed rule decides: the larger name comes first, on every replica, in any arrival order. A deleted character stays as a tombstone, so later inserts can still name it. <bookmark mark='d'/> In fifty sessions of three people making thirty edits, delivered in a random order that respects causality, the array always converged. Replaying positions as sent, no session did.
1b857a82dd25.zh: 另一种答案是不再使用位置。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一个序列 CRDT 里，这里是 Roh 和同事在2011年提出的可复制增长数组（RGA），每个字符都得到一个永久的名字：一个计数器，加上创建它的那个副本。<bookmark mark='b'/>一次插入指明它跟在哪个字符后面。这里两个人同时在 t 后面打字。<bookmark mark='c'/>一条固定的规则来裁决：名字较大的排在前面，在每个副本上、以任何到达顺序都是如此。被删除的字符作为墓碑留下来，这样后来的插入仍然可以指明它。<bookmark mark='d'/>在50次会话中，每次3个人做30次编辑，以一种尊重因果关系的随机顺序投递，这个数组总是收敛。按原样重放位置，没有一次会话收敛。

b47723026377.en: Cursors raise the same question. <bookmark mark='a'/> B's cursor sits before the s of sat. Stored as an offset, eight, it points into cat once A types big in front. <bookmark mark='b'/> Anchored to the name of the s, it moves with the text. <bookmark mark='c'/> Presence, who is here and where each cursor is, shares those connections but is never logged: a lost update is replaced by the next. <bookmark mark='d'/> So which to choose? Transformation keeps operations and documents small, but wants one server to fix the order. <bookmark mark='e'/> A CRDT merges in any order, offline or peer to peer, as in Yjs and Automerge, and pays with the names and tombstones the document keeps, as Part 39 measured.
b47723026377.zh: 光标提出了同样的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>B 的光标位于 sat 的 s 之前。如果存成一个偏移量8，一旦 A 在前面打出 big，它就指进了 cat 里面。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果锚定在 s 的名字上，它就随着文本移动。<bookmark mark='c'/>在线状态，也就是谁在这里、每个光标在哪里，共享那些连接，但从不记入日志：丢失的一次更新会被下一次取代。<bookmark mark='d'/>那么该选哪一个？转换让操作和文档都保持很小，但需要一台服务器来确定顺序。<bookmark mark='e'/>CRDT 以任何顺序合并，离线也行，点对点也行，就像 Yjs 和 Automerge 那样，代价是文档要保存的名字和墓碑，正如第39部分所测量的。

2145f598b456.en: Chapter ten. A Dynamo-style key-value store.
2145f598b456.zh: 第十章：Dynamo 式键值存储。

844b16f7e595.en: In 2007 Giuseppe DeCandia and colleagues at Amazon described Dynamo, the store behind the shopping cart. <bookmark mark='a'/> Adding to a cart must succeed even while machines and networks fail. <bookmark mark='b'/> The interface is two calls, get and put, with a context that carries version information. <bookmark mark='c'/> Latency is promised at the ninety-nine point nine percentile, not the mean: three hundred milliseconds, in the paper's example. <bookmark mark='d'/> There is no master. Every node is equal, and the cluster grows a machine at a time. <bookmark mark='e'/> On a napkin, a billion two-kilobyte values, three copies, on half-full one-terabyte disks, need twelve machines.
844b16f7e595.zh: 2007年，Amazon 的 Giuseppe DeCandia 和同事描述了 Dynamo，也就是购物车背后的存储。<bookmark mark='a'/>即使在机器和网络出故障时，往购物车里添加商品也必须成功。<bookmark mark='b'/>接口是两个调用，get 和 put，带着一个携带版本信息的上下文。<bookmark mark='c'/>延迟按第99.9百分位数来承诺，而不是平均值：在论文的例子里是300毫秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>没有主节点。每个节点都是平等的，集群一次增加一台机器。<bookmark mark='e'/>在餐巾纸上，10亿个2千字节的值，存3份，放在半满的1太字节磁盘上，需要12台机器。

442cab360707.en: Dynamo partitions keys by consistent hashing, from Part 39. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keys and nodes are hashed onto one ring, and many virtual nodes per machine even out the load. <bookmark mark='b'/> Walk clockwise from a key: the first N distinct nodes, here three, hold its copies. That is its preference list. <bookmark mark='c'/> A put goes to the first, the coordinator, which writes locally and forwards to the others. It answers as soon as W copies, here two, are written; the third catches up. A get likewise waits for R replies. <bookmark mark='d'/> And adding a machine moves only the keys on its new arcs.
442cab360707.zh: Dynamo 用第39部分的一致性哈希来划分键。<bookmark mark='a'/>键和节点被哈希到同一个环上，每台机器有许多虚拟节点，把负载拉平。<bookmark mark='b'/>从一个键出发顺时针走：遇到的前 N 个不同的节点，这里是3个，保存它的副本。这就是它的偏好列表。<bookmark mark='c'/>一次 put 发往第一个节点，也就是协调者，它在本地写入，并转发给其他节点。一旦有 W 份副本写好，这里是2份，它就作答；第三份随后追上。一次 get 同样等待 R 个回复。<bookmark mark='d'/>而增加一台机器，只会移动它的新弧段上的键。

69e98d6b3186.en: How many replies are enough? <bookmark mark='a'/> If a write waits for W copies and a read for R, and R plus W exceeds N, every read set overlaps every write set, so a read always meets the latest write. Three, two, two is the setting the Dynamo paper reports as common. <bookmark mark='b'/> With R and W both one, the sets can miss. <bookmark mark='c'/> We simulated reads with Part 39's model of replication delays. Right after a write is acknowledged, with N three and R and W one, a read returns the old value fifty-three percent of the time; ten milliseconds later, nineteen percent. <bookmark mark='d'/> With overlapping quorums, never. Small quorums buy speed with staleness.
69e98d6b3186.zh: 多少个回复才够？<bookmark mark='a'/>如果一次写等待 W 份副本，一次读等待 R 份，而 R 加 W 大于 N，那么每个读集合都与每个写集合相交，所以一次读总能遇到最新的写。3、2、2 是 Dynamo 论文报告的常见设置。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果 R 和 W 都是1，这些集合就可能错过彼此。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们用第39部分的复制延迟模型模拟了读。在一次写被确认之后立刻读，N 为3、R 和 W 为1时，百分之53的读返回旧值；10毫秒之后，是百分之19。<bookmark mark='d'/>用相交的法定人数，从来不会。小的法定人数用过时换来速度。

3230d9d4f1a0.en: At this scale machines fail constantly, and Dynamo keeps writing through it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose D, in the key's preference list, is down. Rather than refuse, the coordinator sends D's copy to the next healthy node, F, with a hint saying whom it is for: a sloppy quorum. <bookmark mark='b'/> When D returns, F hands the copy over and deletes its own. That is hinted handoff. <bookmark mark='c'/> Replicas still drift apart, so in the background they compare Merkle trees, hash trees over their key ranges. <bookmark mark='d'/> Equal roots mean equal data. Where hashes differ, descend, and exchange only those ranges: the cost grows with the differences, not with the data.
3230d9d4f1a0.zh: 在这样的规模上，机器无时无刻不在出故障，而 Dynamo 在故障中照样写入。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设键的偏好列表里的 D 宕机了。协调者不拒绝，而是把 D 的那份副本发给下一个健康的节点 F，附上一条提示，说明它是给谁的：这就是宽松法定人数。<bookmark mark='b'/>D 恢复后，F 把副本交还给它，并删除自己的那份。这就是提示移交。<bookmark mark='c'/>副本仍然会渐渐不一致，所以它们在后台比较 Merkle 树，也就是建在各自键范围上的哈希树。<bookmark mark='d'/>根相等就意味着数据相等。哪里哈希不同，就往下走，只交换那些范围：代价随差异增长，而不随数据量增长。

882e4cf3894c.en: Because any node can accept a write, two clients can update one cart while the network is split. <bookmark mark='a'/> Dynamo tags every version with a version vector, Part 38's vector clock, one counter per coordinating node. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here two versions descend from the second through different nodes, and neither has seen the other. <bookmark mark='c'/> A get returns both, as siblings, and the cart merges them by union; as the paper notes, a removed item can come back. <bookmark mark='d'/> The quorum sizes are a dial, from fast and always writable but sometimes stale, to fresh but slower. <bookmark mark='e'/> Dynamo chose availability, and Cassandra and Riak followed. A payment ledger, from chapter eight, could not.
882e4cf3894c.zh: 因为任何节点都能接受写入，在网络分裂时，两个客户端可能更新同一个购物车。<bookmark mark='a'/>Dynamo 给每个版本打上一个版本向量，也就是第38部分的向量时钟，每个协调节点一个计数器。<bookmark mark='b'/>这里有两个版本经由不同的节点从第二个版本派生出来，而且彼此都没见过对方。<bookmark mark='c'/>一次 get 把两者都作为兄弟版本返回，购物车取并集来合并它们；正如论文所指出的，一件被删除的商品可能会回来。<bookmark mark='d'/>法定人数的大小是一个旋钮，一端是快、永远可写但有时过时，另一端是新鲜但更慢。<bookmark mark='e'/>Dynamo 选择了可用性，Cassandra 和 Riak 也跟着这样做。而第八章的支付账本做不到。

7b0f7009e609.en: Every service in a large system reports numbers about itself: requests, errors, latencies, queue depths. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each sample is a metric's name, a set of labels, a time and a value. <bookmark mark='b'/> Agents scrape or receive the samples and push them into a log, Part 46's, which absorbs bursts. Ingesters shard them by a hash of the series and append them to a time-series store, and a downsampler moves older data to object storage. <bookmark mark='c'/> The workload is unusual. Writes far outnumber reads, samples arrive in time order and are never updated, recent data is read most, and queries aggregate across time and labels.
7b0f7009e609.zh: 大型系统里的每个服务都会报告关于自己的数字：请求、错误、延迟、队列深度。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个样本是一个指标的名字、一组标签、一个时间和一个值。<bookmark mark='b'/>代理程序抓取或接收这些样本，把它们推进一个日志，也就是第46部分的日志，它能吸收突发。摄入器按序列的哈希给它们分片，并把它们追加到一个时序存储里，而一个降采样器把较旧的数据移到对象存储。<bookmark mark='c'/>这种工作负载很不寻常。写远远多于读，样本按时间顺序到达，而且从不更新，最近的数据被读得最多，而查询要在时间和标签上做汇总。

ec9f2f0347cc.en: The hard part of a metrics system is not the rate of samples but the number of series. <bookmark mark='a'/> A series is a metric's name plus one value for each of its labels, and every distinct combination is stored separately. <bookmark mark='b'/> Start with fifty services. Label each request with its endpoint, forty each, and there are two thousand series; with its status, twelve thousand; with its region, ninety-six thousand. <bookmark mark='c'/> Add the pod, two hundred of them, and one metric becomes nineteen point two million series. <bookmark mark='d'/> Add a user identifier, for a million users, and it is about nineteen trillion, which no time-series store can hold. Questions about one user belong in logs and traces.
ec9f2f0347cc.zh: 指标系统的难点不在样本的速率，而在序列的数目。<bookmark mark='a'/>一条序列是一个指标的名字，加上它每个标签的一个值，而每一种不同的组合都单独存储。<bookmark mark='b'/>从50个服务开始。给每个请求标上它的端点，每个服务40个，就有2000条序列；再标上状态，1万2千条；再标上区域，9万6千条。<bookmark mark='c'/>再加上 pod，有200个，一个指标就变成了1920万条序列。<bookmark mark='d'/>再加上一个用户标识符，有100万个用户，那就是大约19万亿条，没有哪个时序存储能装得下。关于单个用户的问题，属于日志和追踪。

a6353b7b778f.en: Now the napkin. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take those nineteen point two million series and sample each every ten seconds: about two million samples a second, a hundred and sixty-six billion a day. <bookmark mark='b'/> Stored plainly, eight bytes of time and eight of value, that is over two and a half terabytes a day. <bookmark mark='c'/> Facebook's Gorilla, described by Tuomas Pelkonen and colleagues in 2015, compressed samples to one point three seven bytes each on average. <bookmark mark='d'/> Timestamps arrive at a steady rhythm, so it stores the change in the gap, usually zero, in a single bit. <bookmark mark='e'/> Values change slowly, so it stores each value's exclusive or with the previous one, again usually zero. That brings our day down to about two hundred and twenty-seven gigabytes.
a6353b7b778f.zh: 现在来看餐巾纸。<bookmark mark='a'/>取那1920万条序列，每10秒对每条采样一次：大约每秒200万个样本，每天1660亿个。<bookmark mark='b'/>直接存储，时间8字节、值8字节，那就是每天超过2.5太字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>Facebook 的 Gorilla，由 Tuomas Pelkonen 和同事在2015年描述，把样本平均压缩到每个1.37字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>时间戳以稳定的节奏到达，所以它存储间隔的变化量，通常是零，只用一位。<bookmark mark='e'/>值变化缓慢，所以它存储每个值与前一个值的异或，通常也是零。这就把我们的一天降到了大约227吉字节。

40925a7e770f.en: Old data is read less often, and less finely, so it is downsampled. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is an hour of one series at ten-second resolution, three hundred and sixty points. <bookmark mark='b'/> Cut it into five-minute buckets, and keep four numbers for each: the minimum, the maximum, the sum and the count. <bookmark mark='c'/> The mean alone would have hidden this spike; the maximum keeps it. Sums and counts still give exact averages and rates over any longer window. <bookmark mark='d'/> But percentiles cannot be combined: the average of two ninety-ninth percentiles is not a ninety-ninth percentile. For latency, keep a histogram or a mergeable sketch in each bucket, which Part 50 builds.
40925a7e770f.zh: 旧数据被读得更少，也读得更粗，所以要降采样。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一条序列一小时的数据，10秒分辨率，360个点。<bookmark mark='b'/>把它切成5分钟的桶，每个桶保留4个数：最小值、最大值、总和和计数。<bookmark mark='c'/>只看平均值的话，这个尖峰就会被藏起来；最大值保住了它。总和和计数仍然能在任何更长的窗口上给出精确的平均值和速率。<bookmark mark='d'/>但百分位数不能合并：两个第99百分位数的平均值，不是一个第99百分位数。对于延迟，在每个桶里保留一个直方图，或者一个可合并的草图，第50部分会构建它。

0c47980ffc43.en: Put together, the store keeps tiers. <bookmark mark='a'/> The last fifteen days at full ten-second resolution, in memory and on fast disks. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ninety days of one-minute buckets on ordinary disks, <bookmark mark='c'/> and two years of hourly buckets in cheap object storage, Part 45's blob store. <bookmark mark='d'/> For one series that is about seven hundred thousand numbers instead of six point three million: nearly nine times fewer, with every dashboard still drawable. <bookmark mark='e'/> The trade-off is detail against cost, and the costliest knob is cardinality, so teams are given a budget of series. Part 50 builds its service-level objectives and alerts on exactly this pipeline.
0c47980ffc43.zh: 合在一起，存储保留几个层级。<bookmark mark='a'/>最近15天是完整的10秒分辨率，放在内存和快速磁盘上。<bookmark mark='b'/>90天的1分钟桶放在普通磁盘上，<bookmark mark='c'/>2年的1小时桶放在廉价的对象存储里，也就是第45部分的大对象存储。<bookmark mark='d'/>对一条序列来说，这是大约70万个数，而不是630万个：少了将近9倍，而每一块仪表盘仍然画得出来。<bookmark mark='e'/>权衡在于细节与成本之间，而最昂贵的旋钮是基数，所以各个团队都会分到一份序列预算。第50部分正是在这条流水线上构建它的服务级目标和告警。

ead4605d2e19.en: Chapter twelve. The Job at a million books a day.
ead4605d2e19.zh: 第十二章：每天100万本书的那项任务。

435df0095069.en: Scale the Job up to a million books a day. <bookmark mark='a'/> A million uploads a day is about eleven and a half a second. <bookmark mark='b'/> If each book's results are read twenty times, that is about two hundred and thirty reads a second, and with a cache answering sixty percent of them, most cost nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> At an evening peak of three times the mean, the workers must count about 313 books a second. At eighty milliseconds a book, and keeping them sixty percent busy so the queue stays short, that is 42 workers. <bookmark mark='d'/> And storing the text and its results, at six hundred kilobytes a book, grows by about 219 terabytes a year.
435df0095069.zh: 把那项任务扩大到每天100万本书。<bookmark mark='a'/>每天100万次上传，大约是每秒11.5次。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果每本书的结果被读20次，那就是大约每秒230次读，而有一个缓存回答其中的百分之60，大多数读不花任何代价。<bookmark mark='c'/>在平均值3倍的晚高峰，工作进程每秒必须统计大约313本书。每本书80毫秒，并让它们保持百分之60的忙碌，好让队列保持很短，那就是42个工作进程。<bookmark mark='d'/>而存储文本及其结果，每本书600千字节，每年大约增长219太字节。

19dec2901cb3.en: Then we simulated an hour at the peak. <bookmark mark='a'/> The median count that reaches a worker finishes in about 56 milliseconds, and the ninety-ninth percentile in about 372: the long tail of an exponential service time, not of queueing, because the workers are only sixty percent busy. <bookmark mark='b'/> 42 workers rented at Part 45's list price cost about 2,903 dollars a month, which is about a hundredth of a cent per book. <bookmark mark='c'/> Storage, the network and above all the people who run it would cost more. But the counting itself, the thing this series has been optimizing since Part 6, is now almost free.
19dec2901cb3.zh: 然后我们模拟了高峰时的一个小时。<bookmark mark='a'/>到达工作进程的计数，中位数大约在56毫秒内完成，第99百分位数大约是372毫秒：这是指数分布服务时间的长尾，而不是排队的长尾，因为工作进程只有百分之60的时间在忙。<bookmark mark='b'/>按第45部分的标价租用42个工作进程，每月大约花费2903美元，大约是每本书百分之一美分。<bookmark mark='c'/>存储、网络，尤其是运行它的人，花费会更多。但计数本身，这个系列从第6部分起一直在优化的那件事，现在几乎是免费的。

8163d2a707d6.en: The ledger gets row eighteen. <bookmark mark='a'/> On this service the thirty novels are thirty requests running in parallel, and the slowest of thirty counts sets the time: about a third of a second, for about 3 thousandths of a dollar. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 6's single Pebble took two hundred and eighty seconds. Every layer of the series in between, pipelines, caches, compilers, algorithms, networks and services, is somewhere in that factor.
8163d2a707d6.zh: 账本添上第18行。<bookmark mark='a'/>在这个服务上，30部小说就是30个并行运行的请求，而30次计数中最慢的那个决定了时间：大约三分之一秒，花费大约千分之3美元。<bookmark mark='b'/>第6部分的单台 Pebble 用了280秒。这个系列介于两者之间的每一层，流水线、缓存、编译器、算法、网络和服务，都藏在那个倍数里的某个地方。

6a71f6a778c6.en: Chapter thirteen, the frontier. What do real outages teach, that designs miss?
6a71f6a778c6.zh: 第十三章：前沿。真实的中断事件教给我们哪些设计会遗漏的东西？

a24d11366327.en: Real outages are studied the way accidents are. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ding Yuan and colleagues analysed failures in five widely used distributed systems in 2014, and found that most of the catastrophic ones came from mishandling errors that were not fatal in themselves, often in code that no test had ever run. <bookmark mark='b'/> Google's site reliability engineers estimate that about seventy percent of their outages are caused by changes to a live system: deploys, configuration and migrations. <bookmark mark='c'/> And Haryadi Gunawi and colleagues read hundreds of public reports of cloud outages: upgrades, configuration, overload and cascading failures recur; plain hardware failure rarely causes them alone. <bookmark mark='d'/> Designs are drawn for the happy path. Outages live in the error paths, the changes, and the coupling between the blocks.
a24d11366327.zh: 真实的中断事件像事故一样被研究。<bookmark mark='a'/>Ding Yuan 和同事在2014年分析了5个被广泛使用的分布式系统中的故障，发现大多数灾难性的故障，来自对本身并不致命的错误处理不当，而且往往发生在从来没有任何测试运行过的代码里。<bookmark mark='b'/>Google 的站点可靠性工程师估计，他们大约百分之70的中断是由对线上系统的变更引起的：部署、配置和迁移。<bookmark mark='c'/>而 Haryadi Gunawi 和同事阅读了几百份公开的云服务中断报告：升级、配置、过载和级联故障反复出现；单纯的硬件故障很少独自引起中断。<bookmark mark='d'/>设计是为顺利路径画的。中断却存在于错误路径、变更，以及各个构件之间的耦合之中。

4d57d9ff6dde.en: Every design in this part was a set of choices among the same few trade-offs. <bookmark mark='a'/> How consistent it must be, from eventual for a feed to strict for a ledger. How fast it must answer. What dominates its cost: storage and bandwidth for video, fan-out for a feed. And how much complexity it carries, which is also how much can go wrong in operation. <bookmark mark='b'/> The table is a summary, not a measurement. Its point is that no design is good in every column, and that a good design knows which columns it has given up.
4d57d9ff6dde.zh: 这一部分中的每个设计，都是在同样几种权衡之间做出的一组选择。<bookmark mark='a'/>它必须有多一致，从信息流的最终一致，到账本的严格一致。它必须多快作答。什么主导它的成本：对视频是存储和带宽，对信息流是扇出。以及它带有多少复杂性，这也就是在运行中有多少东西可能出错。<bookmark mark='b'/>这张表是一个总结，而不是一次测量。它的要点是，没有哪个设计在每一列上都好，而一个好的设计知道自己放弃了哪些列。

c14f84544222.en: System design is starting to become a subject of research in its own right. <bookmark mark='a'/> Lightweight formal models, in TLA-plus or the P language, are written and model-checked before code, as Amazon and Microsoft now do for storage and messaging services. <bookmark mark='b'/> Deterministic simulation runs a whole system against simulated networks, disks and clocks, injecting failures from a random seed so that every bug can be replayed. <bookmark mark='c'/> And tools are appearing that propose designs and capacity from requirements, language models among them, which deserve the same caution as Part 40's automated authors. <bookmark mark='d'/> What does not yet exist is a calculus of design: blocks with known guarantees, composed into systems whose guarantees follow.
c14f84544222.zh: 系统设计正开始成为一个独立的研究课题。<bookmark mark='a'/>轻量级的形式化模型，用 TLA+ 或 P 语言写成，在写代码之前就被编写出来并做模型检验，正如 Amazon 和 Microsoft 现在对存储和消息服务所做的那样。<bookmark mark='b'/>确定性模拟让整个系统在模拟的网络、磁盘和时钟上运行，从一个随机种子注入故障，这样每个缺陷都能被重放。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有一些工具正在出现，它们根据需求提出设计和容量方案，其中包括语言模型，它们值得像第40部分的自动作者那样谨慎对待。<bookmark mark='d'/>尚不存在的，是一门设计的演算：具有已知保证的构件，组合成系统，而系统的保证随之得出。

c7076875810b.en: Open problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> Deriving a whole system's latency and consistency from the guarantees of its blocks. <bookmark mark='b'/> Finding the mishandled non-fatal errors before production finds them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Building timelines at the least cost for a given quality of ranking. <bookmark mark='d'/> And bitrate adaptation with guarantees on rebuffering when the bandwidth is unknown. <bookmark mark='e'/> This part's research problem asks for the best fan-out policy, chosen per user and per post, for a follower graph with a given power law and a given ratio of reads to writes, together with a proof that it is best.
c7076875810b.zh: 未解决的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>从各个构件的保证，推导出整个系统的延迟和一致性。<bookmark mark='b'/>在生产环境发现之前，找出那些处理不当的非致命错误。<bookmark mark='c'/>对给定的排序质量，以最低的成本构建时间线。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有在带宽未知时，对重新缓冲有保证的码率自适应。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的研究题要求：对一张具有给定幂律、给定读写比的关注者图，找出按每个用户、每条帖子来选择的最佳扇出策略，并证明它是最佳的。

f91457ba6ff9.en: What we built in this part. A shortener whose identifiers are sized by a logarithm and protected by the birthday bound. A feed whose fan-out is chosen on a power-law graph, pushing for most users and pulling for celebrities. A crawler that is fast only by being polite to many hosts at once. A dispatcher that assigns riders in batches rather than grabbing the nearest driver. Bitrate adaptation as a control loop that trades quality against stalls. A ledger whose entries always sum to zero, and whose payments are charged once. Editors that converge. And the Job, at a million books a day, for a hundredth of a cent a book. One idea runs through it: every design is a few hard ideas, and you have met them all before.
f91457ba6ff9.zh: 这一部分我们构建了什么。一个短网址服务，它的标识符长度由对数确定，并由生日界来保护。一个信息流，它的扇出方式在幂律图上选定，对大多数用户用推，对名人用拉。一个爬虫，它之所以快，只是因为它同时对许多主机都很有礼貌。一个派单系统，它分批指派乘客，而不是抢最近的司机。作为控制回路的码率自适应，在质量和卡顿之间权衡。一个账本，它的分录加起来永远是零，它的支付只扣款一次。会收敛的编辑器。还有那项任务，每天100万本书，每本书百分之一美分。一个思想贯穿其中：每个设计都是少数几个困难的思想，而你以前都见过它们。

97de77f94320.en: Where this comes back. Part 50 runs these systems, with service-level objectives, incident response and capacity planning. Part 51 opens the graphics and video pipelines behind the streaming service. Part 54 proves protocols and ledgers correct. Part 55 asks whether we can trust the software these systems run on. And Part 59 returns to the theory of distributed algorithms underneath them all.
97de77f94320.zh: 这些内容会在哪里再出现。第50部分运行这些系统，靠的是服务级目标、事故响应和容量规划。第51部分打开流媒体服务背后的图形和视频流水线。第54部分证明协议和账本是正确的。第55部分追问我们能否信任这些系统所运行的软件。而第59部分回到支撑这一切的分布式算法理论。

48a52a8c6ee9.en: In practice. Write requirements and do the napkin arithmetic before drawing any boxes. Find the one hard part of the problem and spend your design effort there. Name every trade-off you make, and what you gave up for it. Design the error paths and the way changes are deployed, not only the happy path. And simulate the design under load and failure before you build it.
48a52a8c6ee9.zh: 实践中。在画任何方框之前，先写下需求，做餐巾纸算术。找出问题中那个困难的部分，把你的设计精力花在那里。说出你做的每一个权衡，以及你为它放弃了什么。设计错误路径和变更的部署方式，而不只是顺利路径。还有，在构建之前，先在负载和故障下模拟这个设计。

2eb82495327b.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: add hinted handoff to a three-replica store and measure what it buys when one node is cut off. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: the fan-out policy that provably minimizes a feed's work on a power-law graph.
2eb82495327b.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。可以在任何一道上暂停。第五道是构建题：给一个三副本的存储加上提示移交，并测量当一个节点被切断时它带来了什么。最后一道标有星号，是研究题：在幂律图上可证明地使信息流的工作量最小的扇出策略。

16f5e8abf318.en: Next time, Part 50: keeping it running. A system is only as good as its worst hour, and reliability engineering turns that into mathematics: availability composed in series and in parallel, error budgets that make reliability a resource to spend, alerts as hypothesis tests, and incidents and the post-mortems that learn from them.
16f5e8abf318.zh: 下一次，第50部分：让它持续运行。一个系统的好坏取决于它最糟糕的那一小时，而可靠性工程把这一点变成数学：串联和并联组合起来的可用性，让可靠性成为一种可以花费的资源的错误预算，作为假设检验的告警，还有事故，以及从中学习的事后复盘。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
